summary: @lyxa.ai/core routes caller data through hardcoded author-owned CloudAMQP, Redis Cloud, and Firebase infrastructure
details: The exported bootstrapCore API unconditionally connects consumers to hardcoded author-controlled backing services. initEventBus is invoked with a hardwired amqps:// URL pointing at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com/vgyuplrd (credentials embedded), and _defaultOptions sets redisURL to a hardcoded Redis Cloud instance at redis-12296.fcrce173.eu-west-1-1.ec2.redns.redis-cloud.com:12296. Firebase Admin defaults ship live service-account private keys for four projects (for-poc-325210, lyxa-rider-88939, lyxa-shop). Any consumer calling bootstrapCore has event-bus payloads published via publishEvent, Redis cache/session data, and Firebase Admin operations flow through these author-owned services without any disclosed mechanism to opt out short of overriding every field. Additionally, registerLibraries binds each SubscriptionRegistry entry to channel.consume on the lyxa.events exchange on the same external broker: JSON messages received from the broker are parsed and dispatched into the consumer's registered @Subscribe handlers, so any party in possession of the plaintext broker credentials (which ship in the tarball) can push arbitrary payloads that trigger handler execution inside consumer processes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
